action_items.text: Come up with a components concept
Look into materials that are durable (symbols won't fade)
Research whether a universal remote control is possible (including mode switching for different TV brands)
Check feasibility of L_C_D screen (text-only preview)
Investigate whether TV menu can be invoked via remote signal
Look into circuit board integration (single board with connections)
Present ideas on paper (shape, curves, colours)
draw some designs for the remote (e.g., layout, buttons, placement)
find out if rechargeable batteries are possible/cost-effective for the remote
find out if L_C_D_ screen is possible/cost-effective for the remote
find out what people are willing to pay for comfort features (e.g., rechargeable batteries, L_C_D_ screen)
research if speech recognition is possible/cost-effective for the remote
research if brightness adjustment (and related menu functions) can be reached via the remote (i.e., via TV menu)
post designs/updates periodically on the product share
draw/work on a small, futuristic design that fits in the hand

decisions.text: Do not implement speech recognition now (technology not mature enough)
Hide less important settings (sound, display) under a menu
Target people under 40; appeal to younger audience with design/covers
Use changeable covers (not full remote redesign); keep basic remote + separate covers
power button should be on top (first thing users do: turn device on)
basic channel buttons (up/down) and volume buttons should be on top/central area, not stacked away
mute button should be at the bottom (often used frequently)
important buttons (power, channel, volume) should be on top; less important (e.g., menu, extra functions) below
L_C_D_ screen (if included) should be placed on top/central area, but may require stacking other buttons below
meeting will be cut now; no decision on final layout; continue discussion later
